title: Open problem: no-kernel lower bound at twin-width 4 for Connected/Total k-Dominating Set
statement_text: Can one show that Connected $k$-Dominating Set and Total $k$-Dominating Set on graphs of twin-width at most $4$ do not admit a polynomial kernel (unless $\mathrm{coNP} \subseteq \mathrm{NP/poly}$), even when a $4$-sequence of the graph is given?
context_text: A partition sequence of an $n$-vertex graph $G$ is a sequence of partitions $\mathcal{P}_n,\dots,\mathcal{P}_1$ of $V(G)$, from all singletons to the single part $V(G)$, each obtained from the previous one by merging two parts. Two parts are homogeneous if either all or none of the pairs between them are edges. A $d$-sequence is a partition sequence in which every part of every $\mathcal{P}_i$ is non-homogeneous to at most $d$ other parts of $\mathcal{P}_i$, and the twin-width of $G$ is the least $d$ admitting a $d$-sequence. A kernel for a parameterized problem is a polynomial-time algorithm mapping each instance to an equivalent instance whose size is bounded by a function of the parameter $k$; it is polynomial if this function is polynomial. Connected $k$-Dominating Set asks for a dominating set of size at most $k$ inducing a connected subgraph, and Total $k$-Dominating Set for a set $D$ of size at most $k$ such that every vertex of $G$ (including those of $D$) has a neighbour in $D$. These problems are FPT on graphs given with an $O(1)$-sequence, by first-order model checking. The authors' main result is that, unless $\mathrm{coNP}\subseteq\mathrm{NP/poly}$, $k$-Dominating Set has no polynomial kernel on graphs of twin-width at most $4$, even when a $4$-sequence is given. Local gadget modifications of this reduction give the same lower bound for Connected $k$-Dominating Set and Total $k$-Dominating Set on graphs of bounded twin-width, but with a worse twin-width bound than $4$; more work would be needed to get it down to $4$. The paper also observes that most optimization and decision graph problems, including $k$-Dominating Set and Connected $k$-Dominating Set, are polynomial-time solvable on graphs of twin-width at most $1$.
notes: Implicit open problem stated in prose: 'More work would be necessary to get the lower bound for twin-width at most 4.' Confirmed by Table 1, which lists no 'no PK' entry for Connected k-Dominating Set at twin-width at most 4. PDF source — math notation may be partially garbled.
